english.title: Assault a boy under 13 years of age by penetration with a part of your body / a thing
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) intentionally penetrated the anus of a boy under the age of 13, namely **(..SPECIFY THE AGE..), with a

(A)_[part of your body, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PART..),]_
(B)_[thing, namely **(..SPECIFY THE THING..),]_
(C)_[part of your body and a thing, namely **(..SPECIFY THE PART OF THE BODY AND THE THING..),]_

and that penetration was sexual
english.legislation: Contrary to section 6 of the Sexual Offences Act 2003.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
intentionally penetrated the anus of a boy under 13 with a part of your body / an object

investigatoraction.description: Attracts liability for entry on sex offenders register
Consider an application for a sexual harm prevention order after conviction

DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) An act done by a person in a country or territory outside the United Kingdom which, constituted an offence under the law in force in that country or territory, and would constitute a sexual offence to which this section applies if it had been done in England and Wales or in Northern Ireland, constitutes that sexual offence under the law of that part of the United Kingdom, and provided that person was on 01/09/1997, or who has since become a British citizen or resident in the United Kingdom he/she may have proceedings brought against them in the United Kingdom. (section 72).
(ii) A person guilty of this offence is subject to notification and orders as provided by section 80 of the Act. (Sch 3 paragraph 19).
(iii) See also offence wordings: H5671 - relating to a girl under 13.
(iv) IMPORTANT - carefully check an offender's previous convictions. A prior conviction for an offence listed in Schedule 15 to the Sentencing Act 2020, may render the convicted person liable to a mandatory life sentence in relation to a second offence listed under that Schedule, as per Section 273 (offender aged 18 or over but under 21 when convicted of the second offence or Section 283 (offender aged 21 or over).

other.penalty:
Indictable only - Life imprisonment

See Note (iii) above re mandatory life sentence

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

libra.complexpenaltydetails: See Note (iii) above re mandatory life sentence
